questions.question: The percentage profit earned by selling an article for ₹6,833 is equal to the percentage loss incurred by selling the same article for ₹1,447. At what price should the article be sold (in ₹) to make a 45% profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Profit% = Loss%** for two selling prices, the **Cost Price (CP)** is the average of those two prices.

CP = (6833 + 1447) ÷ 2 = 8280 ÷ 2 = 4140.

To make a **45% profit**, required SP = CP × 1.45.

SP = 4140 × 145 ÷ 100 = 41.4 × 145 = 6003.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,003.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP₁ = ₹6,833, SP₂ = ₹1,447, Profit% = Loss%, Desired Profit% = 45%.

**Formulas:** CP = (SP₁ + SP₂) ÷ 2 (if Profit% = Loss%), SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/336f369ce82e3cc41ef5f72220d2f3a1e8d2e3b82ebae86fcb84ff53bbb06475.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price** be x.

⇒ Profit% = [(6833 − x) ÷ x] × 100 and Loss% = [(x − 1447) ÷ x] × 100.

⇒ 6833 − x = x − 1447 ⇒ 2x = 8280 ⇒ x = **4140**.

⇒ New Selling Price = 4140 × (100 + 45) ÷ 100 = 4140 × 1.45.

⇒ New SP = **6003**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6,003.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price when Profit = Loss

When numerical profit equals numerical loss for two different selling prices, the CP is always the arithmetic mean of those prices: CP = (SPₕᵢgₕ + SPₗₒw) ÷ 2.

Calculating Profit Selling Price

To calculate a specific profit percentage P%, use the multiplier: SP = CP × (1 + P ÷ 100).

questions.question: The marked price of a wardrobe is ₹668, which is 22% above the cost price. If the profit percentage is 7%, find the discount percentage (rounded off to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the relation between **Marked Price (MP)** and **Cost Price (CP)**: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%).

Ratio of MP to CP is 122 : 100 based on the 22% markup.

122 ÷ 100 = (100 + 7) ÷ (100 − D).

122 × (100 − D) = 107 × 100 ⇒ 12200 − 122D = 10700.

122D = 1500 ⇒ D = 1500 ÷ 122 ≈ 12.295%.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Marked Price (MP)** = ₹668, **Markup** = 22%, **Profit** = 7%.

Formulas: CP = MP × 100 ÷ (100 + Markup%) | SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100 | Discount% = (MP − SP) ÷ MP × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e638858ec0f69fc487deb347c08c94ee7a85f86ac87c718e1bff14e7a071a46e.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** be x. Since MP is 22% above CP, 1.22x = 668 ⇒ x = 668 ÷ 1.22 ≈ 547.54.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = CP × (107 ÷ 100) = 547.54 × 1.07 ≈ 585.87.

⇒ **Discount Amount** = MP − SP = 668 − 585.87 = 82.13.

⇒ **Discount Percentage** = (82.13 ÷ 668) × 100 ≈ 12.295%.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.30%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between CP, MP, Profit and Discount

The most efficient way to solve such problems is the ratio **MP/CP = (100 + P%)/(100 - D%)** which bypasses the need for actual currency values.

Marked Price

It is the price displayed on the product. Discounts are always calculated on the **Marked Price**, while profit or loss is calculated on the **Cost Price**.

questions.question: The selling price of 10 books is equal to the cost price of 16 books. Find the loss or gain percentage.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Selling Price (SP)** to **Cost Price (CP)** can be derived directly: 10 × SP = 16 × CP.

SP/CP = 16/10 = 8/5.

Here, SP (8 units) > CP (5 units), so there is a **gain**.

Gain% = (Difference ÷ CP) × 100 = (8 − 5) ÷ 5 × 100 = 3/5 × 100 = 60%.

**∴ The correct answer is 60% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **SP of 10 books = CP of 16 books**. Formulas: **Profit = SP − CP** | **Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100**.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6a62fdd618c48f038fc757719d799f38ce1a7a046c7fe63a398fded294e8975f.png] 
⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of 1 book be Re. 1.
⇒ Then, **CP of 16 books** = Rs. 16.
⇒ According to the question, **SP of 10 books** = CP of 16 books = Rs. 16.
⇒ **CP of 10 books** = Rs. 10.
⇒ **Gain** = SP − CP = 16 − 10 = Rs. 6.
⇒ **Gain%** = (6 ÷ 10) × 100 = 60%.

**∴ The correct answer is 60% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss on Quantity

When the CP of 'x' articles equals the SP of 'y' articles, the profit or loss percentage is given by [(x − y) ÷ y] × 100. If positive, it is a **gain**; if negative, it is a **loss**.

Relation between SP and CP

If **SP > CP**, there is a profit. If **CP > SP**, there is a loss. Percentage is always calculated on the **Cost Price** unless specified otherwise.</p

questions.question: A dealer marks his goods at 65% above the cost price and allows a discount of 59% on the marked price. What is his gain or loss percentage (correct to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the **Successive Percentage** formula: **Net change = x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100**.

Here, **Markup (x) = +65%** and **Discount (y) = −59%**.

Net percentage = 65 − 59 + (65 × −59) ÷ 100.

Net percentage = 6 − 3835 ÷ 100 = 6 − 38.35 = **−32.35%**.

Since the result is negative, it represents a **loss**.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.35% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Markup = 65%, Discount = 59%.

**Formulas:** MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Loss% = (CP − SP) ÷ CP × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/58cc73505cdebeb7dad9e813bc0dc74240abb33687200b8f4fd4dd47f6fb342d.png] 

⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** be 100.

⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 65% of 100 = 165.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 165 − 59% of 165 = 165 − (59 × 165 ÷ 100) = 165 − 97.35 = 67.65.

⇒ **Loss** = CP − SP = 100 − 67.65 = 32.35.

⇒ **Loss Percentage** = (32.35 ÷ 100) × 100 = 32.35%.

**∴ The correct answer is 32.35% loss.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the **Marked Price (MP)**. The price after applying discount is the **Selling Price (SP)**.

Net Gain or Loss Percentage

When an item is marked up and then a discount is offered, the overall **profit or loss** can be found using the ratio of SP to CP: SP/CP = (100 + m)/100 × (100 − d)/100.</p

Marked Price & Selling Price

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the direct relation between **Cost Price (CP)** and **Marked Price (MP)**: CP ÷ MP = (100 − D%) ÷ (100 + P%).

Given: **Discount (D)** = 22% and **Profit (P)** = 26%.

Ratio CP : MP = (100 − 22) : (100 + 26) = 78 : 126.

Given **CP** = ₹780, which is 78 × 10.

Multiplying the ratio by 10, **MP** = 126 × 10 = ₹1,260.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,260.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **CP** = ₹780, **Profit%** = 26%, **Discount%** = 22%.
Formulas: SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | MP = (SP × 100) ÷ (100 − D%)
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7ab50568de46575b2c69aa5f55e87b78f410aa6620b0b285d9dbdfbae4b0d0e4.png] 
⇒ First, calculate **Selling Price (SP)**: SP = 780 × (126 ÷ 100) = 7.8 × 126 = ₹982.8.
⇒ Now, use the discount to find **Marked Price (MP)**: MP × (100 − 22) ÷ 100 = 982.8.
⇒ MP × 78 ÷ 100 = 982.8.
⇒ MP = (982.8 × 100) ÷ 78 = 98280 ÷ 78.
⇒ MP = ₹1,260.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,260.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

**Marked Price (MP)** is the price listed on the label. Discount is always calculated on MP: SP = MP − Discount.

Cost Price & Profit

**Cost Price (CP)** is the price at which the retailer buys. Profit is always calculated on CP: SP = CP + Profit.

questions.question: A salesman marks his good 64% above the cost price and gives a discount of 25% on them. Find the percentage of this gain or loss.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net Profit% = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100, where a = **Markup%** and b = **Discount%** (negative).

Net Profit% = 64 − 25 − (64 × 25) ÷ 100

Net Profit% = 39 − (1600 ÷ 100)

Net Profit% = 39 − 16 = 23%.

Since the result is positive, it is a **23% gain**.

**∴ The correct answer is 23% gain.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **Markup%** = 64%, **Discount%** = 25%.
Formulas: MP = CP × (100 + Markup%) ÷ 100 | SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100 | Gain% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/520aedd58a09537c668b0cdf096f545a90f6519bc1c077023ab3995b57099327.png] 
⇒ Let **Cost Price (CP)** = 100.
⇒ **Marked Price (MP)** = 100 + 64% of 100 = 164.
⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 164 − 25% of 164 = 164 − (164 ÷ 4) = 164 − 41 = 123.
⇒ **Gain** = SP − CP = 123 − 100 = 23.
⇒ **Gain%** = (23 ÷ 100) × 100 = 23%.

**∴ The correct answer is 23% gain.**

Relation between CP, MP, Discount and Profit

questions.question: Jitesh sold an article at a loss of 11%. If he had bought the item at 5% less and had sold it for ₹739 more, then he would have gained 20%. Find the cost price (in ₹) of the article.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let original **Cost Price (CP₁)** be 100 units.

Original **Selling Price (SP₁)** at 11% loss = 100 − 11 = 89 units.

New **Cost Price (CP₂)** at 5% less = 95 units.

New **Selling Price (SP₂)** at 20% gain = 95 × (120 ÷ 100) = 114 units.

Difference in SP = 114 − 89 = 25 units. Given 25 units = ₹739.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,956.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial loss = 11%, New CP = 95% of original, New Profit = 20%, Price increase = ₹739.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 ± P/L)% | CP = (Difference in SP ÷ Difference in units) × 100.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/aa288345687c9786e6c184da33cba6853a3c40fd925a8544d6fb383e458d579b.png] 

⇒ Let original CP = x.

⇒ Original SP = 0.89x.

⇒ New CP = 0.95x.

⇒ New SP = 0.95x × 1.2 = 1.14x.

⇒ 1.14x − 0.89x = 739.

⇒ 0.25x = 739 ⇒ x = 739 ÷ 0.25 = 2,956.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,956.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change in CP and SP

When both CP and SP change, calculate the new CP first, then apply the profit/loss percentage to find the new SP. The difference between SPs represents the absolute price change.

Unitary Method in Profit and Loss

Assuming base 100 simplifies complex percentage shifts. CP = (Actual Change ÷ Ratio Change) × 100.

questions.question: Three persons X, Y, and Z started a business with their shares in the ratio 3 : 4 : 10. After 6 months, Y withdrew his 50% share, while Z withdrew his 40% share 9 months prior to completion of the year. If the total profit at the end of the year is ₹23,400, find the share of Z (in ₹) in the profit.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Profit** = (Investment × Time).

X: (3 × 12) = 36.

Y: (4 × 6) + (2 × 6) = 24 + 12 = 36.

Z: (10 × 3) + (6 × 9) = 30 + 54 = 84.

Simplified Ratio (X : Y : Z) = 36 : 36 : 84 = **3 : 3 : 7**.

Total parts = 13. Given total profit = **₹23,400**.

Share of Z = (7 ÷ 13) × 23,400 = 7 × 1,800 = **₹12,600**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,600.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given → Initial investment ratio X : Y : Z = 3 : 4 : 10. Total duration = 12 months.
Formulas: Profit Share = Investment × Time Period | Total Profit = Sum of individual shares.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/de9886e9b40cce5fb8497301108338797b30ee55cefc3c436a80a4c3f5b8877c.png] 
→ Let investments be 3k, 4k, and 10k.
→ **X's share** = 3k × 12 = 36k.
→ **Y's share** = (4k × 6) + (2k × 6) = 24k + 12k = 36k.
→ **Z's share**: Withdraws 40% (i.e., 4k) 9 months prior to completion. So, for the first 3 months investment was 10k, and for the remaining 9 months, it was 6k.
→ **Z's share** = (10k × 3) + (6k × 9) = 30k + 54k = 84k.
→ Ratio of shares = 36 : 36 : 84 = 3 : 3 : 7.
→ Sum of ratios = 3 + 3 + 7 = 13.
→ Value of 13 units = 23,400 ⇒ 1 unit = 1,800.
→ Z's share = 7 units × 1,800 = 12,600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹12,600.**

**__Additional Information__**

Partnership Ratio

When investments vary over different time periods, the profit is distributed in the ratio of the product of **Capital and Time**.

Withdrawals and Additions

Any change in capital must be accounted for by splitting the time period into segments where the **effective capital** remains constant.

Total profit in value = 5442 − 4800 = 642.

Total profit % = (642 ÷ 4800) × 100 = 13.375%.

Using **Allegation**: (Profit1: 34%) and (Loss2: −10%) with mean (13.375%).

Ratio of CP = (13.375 − (−10)) : (34 − 13.375) = 23.375 : 20.625 = 187 : 165 = 17 : 15.

Total parts = 17 + 15 = 32. Since 32 parts = 4800, 1 part = 150.

Difference = (17 − 15) × 150 = 2 × 150 = 300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

⇒ 1.34x + 4320 − 0.90x = 5442.
⇒ 0.44x = 5442 − 4320 = 1122.
⇒ x = 1122 ÷ 0.44 = 2550.

⇒ Difference = 2550 − 2250 = 300.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹300.**
